utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Good afternoon, counsel, defendants, all of the technical staff. I'd ask the registrar to call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case number IT-95-16-A, the Prosecutor versus Zoran Kupreskic, Mirjan Kupreskic, Vlatko Kupreskic, Drago Josipovic, and Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you. And now we'll have the appearances starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour, I'm Upawansa Yapa appearing for the Prosecution, with Mr. Norman Farrell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you. And now counsel for Zoran Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ranko Radovic, representing Zoran Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mirjan Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. I'm Jadranka Slokovic-Glumac, representing Mirjan Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Luka Susak, and I am defending Drago Josipovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Anthony Abell representing Vlatko Kupreskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Do we have anyone representing Mr. Santic here? No? All right. Oh, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honour. I'm Petar Pavkovic, and I'm defending Vladimir Santic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Now, as you all know, the Status Conference is convened pursuant to Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the Tribunal, which requires us to have a Status Conference every 120 days primarily to allow the accused to raise any issues relating to their health or conditions of detention, but it is also an opportunity for us to ensure that matters are proceeding expeditiously toward the appeals hearing. So I will take the liberty of telling you what information - excuse me - I presently have about how things are proceeding on this appeal and then we will close by listening to any comments or complaints that the defendants may have. Altogether, it should be a relatively short status hearing. The first item that I would inform you about is that the decision on the matters which were taken up during the oral hearing on the 30th of March will be issued, will be filed with the Registrar and issued by the end of this week, unless something completely unforeseen happens. So it should be available to you by the end of the week, if not sooner. Now, I'm also aware that there are other outstanding Rule 115 motions, among which are the motion filed by Drago Josipovic on the 21st of March, 2001, the Rule 115 motion number 5 filed on 21 March, 2001, by Zoran Kupreskic, and a recently received second Rule 115 motion from Vlatko Kupreskic filed 6th of April, 2001, with a related motion, and all of those are under consideration, and we anticipate that a decision on those motions will be filed next week. So we also have every reason to expect that a decision by the President of the Tribunal will be issued tomorrow, possibly even late today but more probably tomorrow, on whether or not he will authorise the Prosecution to release the Witness AT material to all of the appellants. Now, if he should decide to issue the AT material to all of the appellants under whatever conditions are deemed appropriate, then we will issue a scheduling order promptly thereafter which will inform the parties of the timetable that will have to be observed for filing any Rule 115 motions relating to that material. We are aware of one such motion already filed, and that will be decided at the same time as all of the motions relating to that material that's covered in the President's decision. And I must tell you, that given the expeditious route on which we are embarked, that the parties will be held to strictly comply with those deadlines. Now, as soon as we can, which would be after all of these decisions have been issued - hopefully that would be sometime toward the latter part of next week - a Scheduling Order will be issued which will put forth the timetable for resummation of the briefing schedule, taking into account the fact that there may at that time, there may be, pending 115 motions dealing with material covered by the President's decision, depending on a number of possibilities. So I can indicate to you only the very approximate contours of that timetable, but I will do so just so you have a notion of the route down which we are going, and that would be that supplementary briefs dealing with any new materials which are admitted, either by the decision coming down tomorrow or by any of the other decisions coming down next week, or by the decisions coming down on the 115 motions concerning the AT transcripts and materials, we would expect to have supplementary briefs by approximately May 25th; and then we would ask for the respondents' brief which would be able at that point to take account of all material that will be finally in the appeals record by approximately the 11th of June, with reply briefs about the 26th of June, which would allow us to have oral argument in July and allow us to begin working on the judgement over the holiday, if that's what it is, and get us to the final judgement date sometime in the fall. So that's roughly where we are. You could -- you should expect these various actions which I've laid out within the next week. Of course, you will be informed, but you can be ready to receive and to act thereof. Now, before I move on to the -- asking the appellants about their feelings on any problems that are concerning them in detention, let me let the floor open and see if there are any questions concerning what I'm able to tell you now, which is as much as I am able to tell you now. Let's start with the Prosecution. Anything you wish to raise or any questions you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: At present we do not have any matter to be raised to Your Honour. I must be very thankful to Your Honour for giving all the information. That helps us a great deal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Good. Now, let me go down in the same order that I asked you for your appearances. Let's have counsel for Mr. Zoran Kupreskic first. Mr. Radovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. RADOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as counsel for Zoran Kupreskic, and my colleague, who is representing Mirjan Kupreskic, we are interested in the status of our proposal for the provisional release of Zoran and Mirjan Kupreskic at this point. This is all that we're interest in. We have submitted this motion. We were informed that the Netherlands do not accept their presence here. Bosnia does not accept that either. So we have not received any kind of notification from the Registry regarding this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Well, I can inform you to this degree, Mr. Radovic: We're certainly aware of the motion. It has been under consideration along with the other motions, and you will -- you will hear from us again within the quite near future on that. That's all I'm able to tell you at this time. Ms. Slokovic-Glumac, do you have anything to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we don't have any additional questions at present. The only thing is, of course, we will see, once the final proposal is made of what you have just laid out before us now for the schedule during June and July, then we will see whether it will be possible for us to keep up with that schedule. So far, we are quite satisfied with that suggestion. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: If it's any comfort to you, Ms. Slokovic-Glumac, I sometimes wonder if I can keep up with the schedule that we're setting, but we will do our level best because we all mean to get this appeal done. Now counsel for Mr. Josipovic, Mr. Susak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SUSAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we don't have any questions or remarks. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: And counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic, Mr. Abell.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: No questions or submissions to make. May I thank Your Honour for explaining to us so succinctly and promptly what is your envisaged timetable is. It's most helpful to us. Obviously, we reserve the right, once we've seen it on the paper and in detail, to make written submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: To screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ABELL
utterances.text: I'm sure it won't be screening, Your Honour, but thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: All right. Counsel for Mr. Santic, do you have anything to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence for Vladimir Santic doesn't have any remarks or additional submissions. We are very grateful for all your devotion and desire for an expeditious proceeding. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I will call on the defendants or the appellants themselves and -- to see if -- as you know, one of the purposes of the status hearing is to make sure that we know of any problems the appellants have encountered in detention or otherwise. So I'd start with you, Mr. Zoran Kupreskic. THE APPELLANT Z. KUPRESKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do have one remark. If our counsel don't have anything to say, I do. Recently when we are receiving any kind of decisions by the Appeals Chamber, we either don't receive them at all or we don't receive them in time. As far as I know, in the Statute there is a provision which states that the accused should be informed in the language that he understands about all the things that are happening in the courtroom. Your most recent decision rejecting some evidence which should have been accepted or rejected in accordance with Rule 115, we did not receive it from the Registry at all, and when we did receive it from our counsel, this was already a fait accompli and there was nothing we could do about it. It was closed. Also, whenever we have a Status Conference, we receive the decision on that Status Conference in 10 or 15 days. The ruling, the decision on this Status Conference will be provided to us in 10 or 15 days. I can't believe that there are so many difficulties for us to receive an a document. The decision from the previous Status Conference we only received yesterday, and this is all I have to say at the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I certainly have been listening carefully to your complaint, and at this point, I will simply say that I will look into it. I will find out what the procedures are for having the various documents delivered to the accused in detention. Thank you for your comment. THE APPELLANT Z. KUPRESKIC: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Mirjan Kupreskic. THE APPELLANT M. KUPRESKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am Mirjan Kupreskic. I don't have anything particular to add to what Zoran has already stated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Josipovic. THE APPELLANT JOSIPOVIC: [Interpretation] I am Drago Josipovic, and I don't have any remarks at the moment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic. THE APPELLANT V. KUPRESKIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as the conditions of detention, I have no special remarks to make. Also regarding all the other issues, the only thing that is making me happy is this rather optimistic schedule that you have talked about, and I hope it will be something that's realised. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: I hope so too. And finally, Mr. Santic. THE APPELLANT SANTIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any questions or any remarks. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WALD
utterances.text: Thank you. You obviously are a very cooperative group of defendants. I, too, hope that we will be able to keep to a schedule and get this matter finally judged in the optimal amount of time. I don't have anything else, and I think we can adjourn the Status Conference. I will make some inquiries to see if I can find out what exactly the system is of getting you informed of various decisions. Otherwise, I would suggest everybody just keeps their eyes and ears open for a barrage of impending decisions which should be coming down within the next week. Thank you very much and the Status Conference is adjourned.
